external_entities.name: member
external_entities.description: A grocery loyalty programme member who uses the mobile app and browser sign-in.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Members collect points when they shop and spend them on gift cards.

external_entities.name: member phone
external_entities.description: A phone used by a member to run the mobile app and retain its refresh token.
external_entities.source_excerpt: The app keeps a refresh token on the phone.

processes.name: mobile app
processes.description: The mobile application that signs members in, calls the rewards API, and supports partner disconnection.
processes.notes: PKCE challenge status is not recorded.

processes.name: authorization server
processes.description: The authorization server that signs members in, issues authorization codes and tokens, handles consent, and supports partner authorization.
processes.source_excerpt: The app signs a member in through our authorization server with the authorization code flow

processes.name: rewards API
processes.description: The API that accepts access tokens and reads and writes the points ledger.
processes.source_excerpt: The rewards API reads and writes the points ledger
processes.notes: It does not check which client or audience a token was issued for.

processes.name: partner app
processes.description: A web application run by another company that obtains tokens and can show a member's points.
processes.source_excerpt: Partner apps are web applications that other companies run on their own servers
processes.notes: The text refers to partner apps generically; this model represents that generic partner-app type.

processes.name: browser
processes.description: A browser used to sign in, approve consent, and return an authorization code to a partner app.
processes.source_excerpt: A member who connects a partner app signs in on the authorization server's sign-in page in their browser

processes.name: support console
processes.description: A web application that closes a member's account.
processes.source_excerpt: The support console is a web app that closes a member's account.
processes.notes: It is served on the same public hostname as the rewards API.

data_stores.name: identity database
data_stores.description: The database containing member accounts, email addresses, password hashes, authorization codes, refresh tokens, consents, and account-closure state.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The authorization server keeps member accounts, email addresses and password hashes in the identity database

data_stores.name: points ledger
data_stores.description: The ledger containing every member's balance and every points transaction.
data_stores.source_excerpt: the points ledger, which holds every member's balance and every points transaction

data_stores.name: API log store
data_stores.description: The store containing every request received by the rewards API, including headers.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The rewards API also writes every request it receives, headers included, to the API log store.

data_flows.name: use app
data_flows.description: A member uses the mobile app.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Members use our mobile app.
data_flows.data_description: Member interaction with the mobile app

data_flows.name: approve consent
data_flows.description: A member signs in and approves the partner-app consent screen in a browser.
data_flows.source_excerpt: A member who connects a partner app signs in on the authorization server's sign-in page in their browser and approves a consent screen

data_flows.name: authorize member
data_flows.description: The mobile app signs a member in through the authorization server using the authorization code flow.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The app signs a member in through our authorization server with the authorization code flow
data_flows.notes: The app's PKCE challenge status is not recorded.
data_flows.data_description: Member authorization request and authorization code flow

data_flows.name: disconnect partner
data_flows.description: The mobile app requests disconnection of a partner app, deleting its refresh token.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Members can disconnect a partner app from the settings screen of the mobile app, which deletes that app's refresh token from the identity database.

data_flows.name: call rewards API
data_flows.description: The mobile app calls the rewards API with an access token.
data_flows.source_excerpt: then calls the rewards API with the access token it gets back
data_flows.data_description: Rewards API requests and access token

data_flows.name: sign in
data_flows.description: The browser accesses the authorization server's sign-in page and consent screen.
data_flows.source_excerpt: signs in on the authorization server's sign-in page in their browser and approves a consent screen

data_flows.name: return code
data_flows.description: The authorization server returns an authorization code through the browser.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The browser then returns to the partner app's redirect URI with an authorization code.
data_flows.notes: The browser-mediated redirect is represented as a server-initiated flow to the browser.

data_flows.name: send code
data_flows.description: The browser returns the authorization code to the partner app's redirect URI.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The browser then returns to the partner app's redirect URI with an authorization code.

data_flows.name: request tokens
data_flows.description: The partner app sends its client secret in token requests to the authorization server.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The partner app sends that secret in the body of its token requests.
data_flows.notes: The partner app uses a client ID and client secret.
data_flows.data_description: Token request containing client credentials and authorization code

data_flows.name: show points
data_flows.description: A partner app calls the rewards API to show a member's points.
data_flows.source_excerpt: such as a meal-planning service that shows a member's points

data_flows.name: request token
data_flows.description: The support console obtains access tokens from the authorization server.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The support console is a web app that closes a member's account. It takes access tokens from the same authorization server

data_flows.name: close account
data_flows.description: The support console marks a member's account closed in the identity database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Closing an account marks it closed in the identity database.

data_flows.name: manage identity data
data_flows.description: The authorization server reads and writes identity data, authorization codes, refresh tokens, and consents.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The authorization server keeps member accounts, email addresses and password hashes in the identity database, together with the authorization codes, refresh tokens and consents it issues.
data_flows.data_description: Accounts, email addresses, password hashes, authorization codes, refresh tokens, consents, and account state

data_flows.name: update ledger
data_flows.description: The rewards API reads and writes the points ledger.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The rewards API reads and writes the points ledger

data_flows.name: write request logs
data_flows.description: The rewards API writes every received request, including headers, to the API log store.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The rewards API also writes every request it receives, headers included, to the API log store.

trust_boundaries.name: cloud account
trust_boundaries.description: The organisation's own cloud account where the system components and stores described below run.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Everything below runs in our own cloud account

trust_boundaries.name: member phones
trust_boundaries.description: Members' phones, which are outside the organisation's cloud account and retain mobile refresh tokens.

trust_boundaries.name: partner servers
trust_boundaries.description: Servers run by other companies for their partner applications.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Partner apps are web applications that other companies run on their own servers

assumptions.assumption: The identity database is confidential because it contains member identity data, password hashes, authorization codes, refresh tokens, and consents.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the identity database holds member accounts, email addresses, password hashes, authorization codes, refresh tokens, and consents.

assumptions.assumption: The points ledger is confidential because it contains member balances and points transactions.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the points ledger holds every member's balance and every points transaction.

assumptions.assumption: The API log store is confidential because it contains every request received by the rewards API, including headers.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the rewards API writes every request it receives, headers included, to the API log store.
